paper_title: A new model for learning in graph domains
abstract: This paper presents a new neural model, called graph neural network (GNN), capable of directly processing graphs. GNNs extends recursive neural networks and can be applied on graphs with cyclic connections. The model implements a learning function τ that maps a graph G and one of its nodes n to a vector of reals.

problem.core_question: How to create a neural network that can directly process graph-structured data?
problem.background: Before this work, neural networks were primarily designed for grid-like data (images) or sequential data (text). Graph-structured data posed unique challenges due to its arbitrary topology.
limitations_of_prior: Existing models couldn't handle cyclic graph structures
Recursive neural networks were limited to directed acyclic graphs
No unified framework for learning on general graph structures
problem.motivation: Many real-world problems involve relationships between entities that are naturally represented as graphs (social networks, molecular structures, web pages)

contributions.title: Graph Neural Network (GNN) Model
contributions.description: Introduced the first neural network architecture capable of processing general graph structures with cycles
contributions.novelty: First model to extend recursive neural networks to handle cyclic graph structures
contributions.impact: Foundation for modern graph neural networks, cited over 3000 times

contributions.title: State-Based Computation
contributions.description: Proposed a computation model where each node maintains a state that is updated based on neighbor information
contributions.novelty: Introduced iterative message passing framework for graphs
contributions.impact: Established the core paradigm for message passing in GNNs

contributions.title: Learning Function τ
contributions.description: Defined a learning function that maps (G, n) → R^m for graph-node pairs
contributions.novelty: Formalized graph learning as function approximation on graph-node pairs
contributions.impact: Provided theoretical foundation for graph representation learning

method.overview: The GNN model uses an iterative approach where each node computes its state based on its current state and the states of its neighbors. The process continues until convergence, at which point the final states are used to compute output values.

pros: First general-purpose neural network for graphs
cons: Computationally expensive due to iterative convergence

connections: Precursor to modern Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN)
Inspired message passing paradigm in GNNs
improvements: Batch processing and sampling improved scalability
insights.relevance_to_my_work: This paper establishes the fundamental concept of residual-like learning in graphs through iterative state updates. The cross residual connections in modern GNNs can be seen as an evolution of the state transition mechanism proposed here.

paper_title: Semi-supervised classification with graph convolutional networks
paper_title_zh: 基于图卷积网络的半监督分类
abstract: We present a scalable approach for semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data that is based on an efficient variant of convolutional neural networks. The proposed model learns graph neural networks by stacking layers of graph convolution, which can be interpreted as a first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions.

problem.core_question: How to perform semi-supervised node classification on graph-structured data efficiently?
problem.background: Many real-world datasets have limited labels but rich relational structure (e.g., citation networks, social networks).
limitations_of_prior: Existing spatial methods lacked theoretical foundation
No efficient way to combine graph structure and node features
problem.motivation: Need for simple, scalable, and theoretically grounded approach for graph-based semi-supervised learning

contributions.title: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)
contributions.description: Introduced a simple and efficient layer-wise propagation rule for graph neural networks
contributions.novelty: First-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions that avoids eigen-decomposition
contributions.impact: Most influential GNN paper with 53,000+ citations, became standard baseline

contributions.title: Simplified Spectral Propagation
contributions.description: Showed that graph convolution can be simplified to neighborhood aggregation with renormalization trick
contributions.novelty: Renormalization trick: D~^(-1/2) Ã D~^(-1/2) instead of D^(-1/2) A D^(-1/2)
contributions.impact: Made GCNs computationally efficient and easy to implement

contributions.title: End-to-End Learning
contributions.description: Enabled semi-supervised learning where loss is computed on labeled nodes and gradients propagate through graph structure
contributions.novelty: Joint optimization of node representations and classifier
contributions.impact: Established standard paradigm for graph semi-supervised learning

method.overview: GCN uses a simple layer-wise propagation rule: H^(l+1) = σ(D~^(-1/2) Ã D~^(-1/2) H^(l) W^(l)). Multiple layers are stacked to aggregate information from multi-hop neighborhoods.

experiments.results: GCN achieved state-of-the-art on all datasets with significantly faster training

improvements: Residual connections added for deeper networks
insights.relevance_to_my_work: GCN's simple neighborhood aggregation is the foundation for most modern GNNs. Cross residual connections can be integrated into GCN layers to enable deeper architectures and mitigate over-smoothing.

abstract: We present graph attention networks (GATs), novel neural network architectures that operate on graph-structured data, leveraging masked self-attentional layers. The layers use attention to compute weighted sums of neighborhood features, allowing the model to focus on different aspects of the neighborhood.

problem.core_question: How to enable GNNs to learn importance weights for different neighbors during aggregation?
problem.background: GCN treats all neighbors equally, but in many graphs, some neighbors are more important than others.
limitations_of_prior: GCN uses fixed weights based on graph structure
Cannot learn which neighbors are more relevant
problem.motivation: Need for adaptive, learnable aggregation that can focus on relevant neighbors and features

contributions.title: Graph Attention Network (GAT)
contributions.description: Introduced attention mechanism to graph neural networks, allowing nodes to attend to their neighbors differently
contributions.novelty: First application of self-attention to graph-structured data
contributions.impact: 19,000+ citations, established attention as standard component in GNNs

contributions.title: Multi-Head Attention
contributions.description: Extended the multi-head attention concept from transformers to graphs
contributions.novelty: Independent attention heads learn different aspects of relationships

contributions.title: Efficient Computation
contributions.description: Showed that attention coefficients can be computed efficiently using shared linear transformations
contributions.novelty: Single-pass attention computation without expensive pairwise operations
contributions.impact: Made attention mechanisms scalable to large graphs

method.overview: GAT uses attention to compute coefficients α_ij for each edge (i,j). The final output is a weighted sum: h_i' = σ(Σ_j∈N(i) α_ij W h_j). Multi-head attention is used to stabilize learning.
key_formulas: Multi-head: h_i' = ||_k=1^K σ(Σ_j∈N(i) α_ij^k W^k h_j)

experiments.results: GAT achieved state-of-the-art on transductive node classification and competitive on graph classification

pros: Applicable to both node and graph tasks
cons: Still limited by over-smoothing in deep layers

connections: Built on self-attention from Vaswani et al. (Transformer)
Related to attention mechanisms in computer vision and NLP
improvements: Graph Transformers scaled attention to full graph
insights.relevance_to_my_work: Attention mechanisms complement residual connections well. Cross residual connections can help maintain gradient flow in deep GAT networks, while attention ensures relevant information is preserved across layers.
